\n <div><h2>Как это работает</h2>\n:
How it works

At rest the inside of a neuron is at about −70 mV. This charge is maintained by the Na⁺/K⁺ pump and potassium leak channels.

Signals from the dendrites summate on the cell body. If the charge at the axon hillock reaches threshold (about −50 mV), fast Na⁺ channels open and an action potential fires: sodium rushes in, the charge shoots up to +30 mV, then potassium flows out and restores the negative charge.

Why myelin

Myelin is insulation made by glial cells. The channels are clustered at the nodes of Ranvier, and the impulse jumps from node to node. Turn myelin off and the impulse will creep along as a continuous wave, several times slower.

Local anesthesia

Lidocaine and procaine plug Na⁺ channels. In the treated segment the impulse dies out, and the pain signal never reaches the brain.

What is accurate here

  • The shape of the potential at the electrode: −70 → +30 → −80 mV, threshold about −50.
  • The order of events: summation, hillock, Na⁺ influx, K⁺ efflux.
  • Saltatory conduction and sodium channel block.

Simplifications

  • Time is slowed down roughly a thousandfold.
  • The ions are drawn huge, and the axon is greatly shortened.

\n <div><h2>Как это работает</h2>\n:
How it works

Synthesis. Enzymes in the terminal make the neurotransmitter, and it is packed into vesicles.

Release. The impulse (bright ring) arrives at the terminal and opens Ca²⁺ channels. Calcium makes docked vesicles fuse with the membrane.

Receptor. The molecules cross the cleft and bind to receptors. Ionotropic receptors are channels themselves: Na⁺ (orange) or Cl⁻ (green) passes through them. Metabotropic receptors activate a G protein beneath the membrane and second messengers.

Inactivation. Glutamate is taken up by astrocytes, acetylcholine is cleaved by an enzyme in the cleft, and monoamines and GABA are returned to the terminal by transporters.

Drugs

Switch drugs on and watch the graph: an agonist opens receptors by itself, an antagonist (gray balls) occupies them and keeps the neurotransmitter out, a reuptake blocker keeps molecules in the cleft, and an enhancer makes each response stronger.

  • The order of events and the role of calcium.
  • The receptor type and the inactivation route for each neurotransmitter.
  • The mechanisms of the drugs from the course.

Simplifications

  • One ball stands for many molecules: a vesicle holds thousands.
  • The cleft is enlarged and time is slowed: in reality it all takes milliseconds.

\n <div><h2>Как это устроено</h2>\n:
How it is organized

Glutamate and GABA are found almost everywhere and carry the signal itself. The five systems in this model work differently: a few thousand or tens of thousands of cells in a single nucleus control the mood, attention, sleep and movement of the whole brain.

Dopamine pathways

Nigrostriatal: from the substantia nigra to the striatum, movement. Mesolimbic: from the tegmentum to the nucleus accumbens, pleasure and motivation. Mesocortical: to the frontal cortex, attention and planning. Tuberoinfundibular: to the pituitary, keeps prolactin in check.

Why it matters

Antidepressants, antipsychotics, stimulants and sleeping pills act on these systems. That is why their effects are so broad: they change the activity of the entire cortex at once.

  • The location of the source nuclei: brainstem, midbrain, hypothalamus, base of the forebrain.
  • Where the projections of each system go.

  • The brain is a simplified model with gyri, not a scan.
  • Real projections number in the millions; here there are about ten per system.

\n <div><h2>Как устроена клетка</h2:
How a cell is built

A neuron is a cell like any other, just with very long processes. Everything discussed in the course starts here: receptor proteins and channels are made on the rough ER, finished in the Golgi apparatus and carried to the membrane in vesicles.

What moves

Blue vesicles carry proteins from the ER to the Golgi. Gold ones go from the Golgi to the membrane and fuse with it — this is exocytosis, the same mechanism a synapse uses to release a neurotransmitter. Lilac ones pinch off from the membrane and drift to the lysosomes. Along the microtubules motor proteins carry cargo in both directions. mRNAs exit the nuclear pores, and ATP flashes at the mitochondria.

Energy

The brain is about 2% of body mass but uses roughly 20% of the energy. Most of the ATP is consumed by the Na⁺/K⁺ pump, which is why neurons have so many mitochondria.

What is accurate here

  • The set of organelles and their arrangement: the ER is continuous with the nuclear envelope, and the Golgi lies next to the centrosome.
  • The double nuclear envelope with pores, mitochondrial cristae, 9 microtubule triplets in the centrioles.
  • The routes of the vesicles.

Simplifications

  • Sizes are not to scale: a ribosome is a thousand times smaller than the cell, yet here you can see it.
  • A real cell has hundreds of times more organelles and ribosomes.

\n <div><h2>Как устроен скелет</h2>:
How the skeleton is built

An adult has 206 bones. The axial skeleton — skull, spine and rib cage — protects the brain, spinal cord, heart and lungs. The appendicular skeleton — the girdles and limbs — is responsible for movement.

Muscles

The body has about 640 skeletal muscles; they make up roughly 40% of body mass in men and about 30–35% in women. A muscle is attached by tendons (pale bands) to two bones and can only pull, so muscles work in pairs: the biceps flexes the arm at the elbow, the triceps extends it. Each muscle is controlled by motor neurons of the spinal cord, and the signal is transmitted by acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction.

Circulatory system

The heart beats about 70 times a minute. Arteries (red) carry blood away from the heart, veins (blue) return it. In the pulmonary circulation it is the other way round: the pulmonary trunk carries dark blood to the lungs (blue), and the pulmonary veins return scarlet blood. Pale waves show the direction of flow. Turn on “X-ray” to see the vessels through the bones.

Link to the nervous system

The brain lies in the skull, the spinal cord in the vertebral canal. Nerves exit between the vertebrae, which is why a herniated disc can press on a nerve root and cause pain in an arm or leg.

Bone is living tissue

Bones hold about 99% of the body’s calcium. When blood Ca²⁺ runs low, it is taken from the bones, and without calcium not a single synapse works. Blood cells are made in the red bone marrow.

\n <div><h2>Как устроен нейрон</h2>:
How a neuron is built

A neuron has a cell body (soma) with a nucleus and ribosomes, where proteins are synthesized, and two kinds of processes. Dendrites receive signals and carry them to the cell body. The cell body sums excitatory and inhibitory inputs and decides whether to fire a response. The axon carries the impulse away to other cells. The axon leaves the cell body at a site called the axon hillock.

Dendrite and axon

A dendrite is shorter (about 0.5–1 mm), branches at acute angles and tapers like a tree branch. An axon is from centimeters to a meter or more long. It keeps a constant diameter of 0.5–1.5 µm and branches at right angles: collaterals copy the signal to several targets. Dendrites in the CNS are usually unmyelinated, axons are often myelinated. Nissl substance is present in dendrites but absent from the axon.

Three functional classes

Sensory (afferent) neurons sit at the input, interneurons link input to output, and in a complex nervous system they are the most numerous. Effector (efferent) neurons sit at the output: motor neurons control muscles, autonomic neurons control organs.

How cells were first seen

In 1836 Purkinje fixed the soft tissue of the cerebellum and made out large cells. Golgi invented silver staining, Ramón y Cajal drew the finest branchings and synapses, and both received the 1906 Nobel Prize. Nissl stained ribosomes with methylene blue.

What is accurate here

  • The number and arrangement of processes in each shape.
  • Acute branching angles in dendrites, right angles in axon collaterals.
  • The flat tree of the Purkinje cell, the spines of the pyramidal neuron, the T-shaped process of the sensory neuron.
  • The look of the stains: a black silhouette on orange, Nissl substance only in the cell body and dendrite bases.

Simplifications

  • Cell sizes are equalized, and axons are greatly shortened.
  • The impulse is slowed roughly a thousandfold.
  • The Golgi method stains only some cells; here all of them are stained.

<b>Астроциты</b>: самые крупные и многоч: Astrocytes are the largest and most numerous glial cells. They pack the fine web of axons and dendrites so that the brain can withstand concussions. Their end feet completely sheathe the capillaries and form the blood–brain barrier. Astrocytes take up and break down neurotransmitters after the synapse, regulate ions and water, and form a scar after injury.
<b>Олигодендроцит</b> («клетка с немноги: An oligodendrocyte (“cell with few processes”) insulates neurons from one another. Each process wraps around its own axon, up to 100 layers of membrane, forming a myelin sheath about 1 mm long. Bare nodes of Ranvier remain between the sheaths, and the impulse jumps from node to node: 100–120 m/s instead of 1–5. In the periphery the same job is done by Schwann cells, which have one process per sheath.
<b>Микроглия</b>: самые маленькие глиаль: Microglia are the smallest glial cells, the resident macrophages of the brain. Unlike the rest of the glia, they come from the mesoderm. At rest their thin processes “listen” to synapses, and microglia can tear down a weak synapse: this is pruning, trimming of the network. After injury or during inflammation the cells enlarge, divide, move to the lesion and devour the debris.
<b>Эпендимоциты</b> выстилают одним слое: Ependymal cells line the cavities of the brain in a single layer: the four ventricles, the cerebral aqueduct and the central canal of the spinal cord. In early stages their cilia drive the CSF; in adults they remain only in places. The ependyma takes part in exchange between the blood, the CSF and the brain.
<b>Нейроны</b> передают информацию, глия: Neurons transmit information, and glia help them work. After birth neurons almost never divide (exceptions: the hippocampus and the olfactory centers), while glia divide throughout life. In the neocortex there is one glial cell per neuron, in the medulla oblongata up to ten.
<b>Миелинизация.</b> Отросток олигодендр: Myelination. A process of the oligodendrocyte flattens into a thin tongue and wraps around a bare axon again and again. The membrane layers stick together, the cytoplasm is squeezed out of them, and a dense white sleeve forms. In the CNS this is done by the oligodendrocyte (one cell serves many axons), in the periphery by the Schwann cell.
Слабых синапсов не осталось: микроглия у: No weak synapses are left: microglia have already removed them. Reload the scene to start over.
<b>Прунинг</b> («обрезка»). Этот синапс: Pruning (“trimming”). This synapse barely works: only occasional flashes. Weak contacts are tagged with complement proteins (red glow), and microglia recognize them by this tag.
<b>Готово: 7 слоёв мембраны.</b> Теперь: Done: 7 layers of membrane. Now current no longer leaks through the membrane, and the impulse jumps from one node of Ranvier to the next (yellow spark on the neighboring axon). Speed rises from 0.5–2 m/s in a bare fiber to 100 m/s and more. In humans myelination goes on for about 20 years: the spinal cord first, the frontal cortex last of all.
<b>Синапс съеден.</b> Микроглия перевари: Synapse eaten. The microglial cell digested the bouton in its lysosomes and returned to its place. Strong, frequently used contacts remain. In childhood and adolescence up to half of all cortical synapses are removed this way: the brain keeps the connections it needs and saves energy. Pruning defects have been linked to autism and schizophrenia.
Четыре типа глии вокруг двух нейронов. В: Four types of glia around two neurons. Select a cell to make the others transparent. Every few seconds glutamate from protein food enters the blood: with the BBB closed, it floats past.
<b>Травма.</b> Микроглия чувствует проду: Injury. Microglia sense the breakdown products of cells, grow, divide and crawl to the lesion. There they engulf the debris (phagocytosis) and release inflammatory signaling molecules.
Glia по-гречески «клей». Глия упаковывае: Glia is Greek for “glue”. Glia pack neurons, insulate them, guard the entry from the blood and clear away debris.
\n <div><h2>Зачем нейронам глия</h2:
Why neurons need glia

Glial cells were discovered by Rudolf Virchow, and the word “neuroglia” was introduced by Golgi. Glia fill all the space between neurons. In the neocortex there is one glial cell per neuron, in the medulla oblongata up to ten. Gliocytes are 3–4 times smaller than neurons, contain little Nissl substance, form no synapses and do not transmit signals electrically.

Blood–brain barrier

Astrocyte end feet sheathe the capillary completely, and substances from the blood reach the brain only through them. Glutamate is the main excitatory neurotransmitter and at the same time the most common amino acid in food. Without the barrier, any protein meal would overexcite the brain. Turn off “BBB” and see what happens to the neurons.

White and gray matter

Myelin is 75% lipid, with a lot of cholesterol, and is therefore white. Bundles of myelinated axons form the white matter, the “wiring”. The cell bodies and dendrites of neurons form the gray matter. In multiple sclerosis the immune system attacks myelin protein. Myelination proceeds over the first 20 years of life, from the spinal cord to the cortex, and the corpus callosum begins it only in the second month after birth.

Where glia come from

Astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and ependymal cells develop from the neuroectoderm. Microglia are mesodermal: during embryogenesis phagocyte precursor cells enter the brain and stay there.

What is accurate here

  • The four types of glia and where they sit: end feet on the capillary, sheaths on different axons from a single oligodendrocyte, branching microglia near synapses, a single-layered ciliated ependyma.
  • Nodes of Ranvier between the sheaths and the jumping impulse.
  • The microglial response to injury: growth, division, movement to the lesion, phagocytosis.

Simplifications

  • Scales are brought closer together: in reality the capillary is narrower than a neuron’s cell body, and a sheath is about 1 mm long.
  • Glutamate is drawn as large dots.

На спинной стороне зародыша часть клеток: On the dorsal side of the embryo some ectoderm cells become the neural plate. The entire central nervous system will develop from it: both the brain and the spinal cord.
Края пластинки поднимаются в <b>нервные: The edges of the plate rise into neural folds, with a groove left between them. Around day 20 the edges meet in the middle of the embryo, and the seam spreads forward and backward like a zipper. Cells from the edges form the neural crest (orange sparks): they will leave the tube and give rise to ganglia, the pia and arachnoid mater, pigment cells and the adrenal medulla.
К концу 4-й недели трубка замкнута целик: By the end of week 4 the tube is completely closed, including the anterior and posterior neuropores. A canal remains inside. Genes have already decided what the cells will become: the upper alar plate will give rise to sensory neurons and interneurons, the lower basal plate to motor and autonomic neurons. Switch the coloring to “Plates”.
Передний конец трубки раздувается в три: The front end of the tube swells into three vesicles: the forebrain (prosencephalon), midbrain (mesencephalon) and hindbrain (rhombencephalon). The rest of the tube will become the spinal cord. The optic vesicles bulge out of the forebrain wall: the retina is actually part of the diencephalon.
Передний пузырь даёт <b>конечный</b> моз: The forebrain vesicle gives rise to the telencephalon (the future hemispheres) and the diencephalon (thalamus and hypothalamus). The midbrain barely changes. The hindbrain divides into the metencephalon proper (pons and cerebellum) and the myelencephalon (medulla oblongata). The tube bends: first the cephalic flexure, then the cervical, and last the pontine.
Нейроны рождаются в первые 16 недель: сн: Neurons are born in the first 16 weeks: first the deep layers of the cortex, the sixth and fifth, then the upper ones. The cells crawl to their places along the processes of radial glia, guided by netrins, ephrins and semaphorins. By week 20 migration is complete, the lobes take shape and sulci begin to form. The hemispheres grow fastest of all and cover the diencephalon, midbrain and hindbrain.
К 9 месяцам видна привычная архитектура:: By 9 months the familiar architecture is visible: sulci, gyri, cerebellum. The brain weighs about 350 g. There will be no more new neurons: from now on the dendritic trees, the synapses and the number of glial cells grow.
Взрослый мозг весит <b>1300–1400 г</b> п: The adult brain weighs 1300–1400 g with the same number of neurons. The gain comes from dendritic branching, new synapses, glia and myelin, and myelination lasts about 20 years. The first 2–3 years are especially important: how many connections form depends on how curious the child is and how much people engage with them.

\n <div><h2>Как развивается мозг</h:
How the brain develops

Embryogenesis is part of ontogenesis, the organism’s path from conception to death. Behind it lies a cascade of genes switching on and off: they control cell division, cell movement, where cells end up, what kind of neuron a cell becomes and which neurotransmitter it releases.

Neurulation

The ectoderm on the dorsal side gives rise to the neural plate, which folds into a groove and closes into a tube. The wall of the tube is neuroepithelium around a canal. Cells next to the canal divide into spongioblasts and neuroblasts. Spongioblasts extend radial processes to the outer surface, and neurons migrate along them. Later the spongioblasts give rise to glia: ependyma, astrocytes and oligodendrocytes. Neurogenesis comes first, then gliogenesis.

Vesicles

3 vesicles → 5: forebrain → telencephalon (hemispheres and subcortical nuclei) + diencephalon (thalamus, hypothalamus); midbrain → tectum (corpora quadrigemina) and cerebral peduncles; hindbrain → metencephalon (pons, cerebellum) + myelencephalon (medulla oblongata).

After birth

Mass grows from 350 to 1300–1400 g, but the number of neurons does not. Dendrites, synapses, glia and myelin grow. The most important years are the first 2–3: how many connections form depends on the environment and on interaction with others.

What is accurate here

  • The order and timing of stages: closure from day 20, the tube by the end of week 4, 5 vesicles by weeks 5–6, neurogenesis until week 16, migration until week 20.
  • Closure from the middle toward the ends, the neural crest along the edges.
  • The alar and basal plates, the order of the flexures.

Simplifications

  • All stages are shown at the same size, although the brain grows hundreds of times larger.
  • The shapes of the vesicles and flexures are simplified.
  • The scale on the right shows the processes; the line marks the current age.

Все четыре пучка целы: каждый глаз видит: All four fiber bundles are intact: each eye sees the whole field, and both halves of the field reach the cortex.
<b>Повреждён правый зрительный нерв</b>: Right optic nerve damaged (before the chiasm). The right eye goes completely blind, the left one sees the whole field. This happens with optic neuritis or nerve injury.
<b>Повреждён перекрёст (хиазма).</b> Рву: Optic chiasm damaged. Only the crossing fibers from the nasal halves of the retinas are cut, and they see the temporal halves of the field. Both outer halves are lost: bitemporal hemianopia, “blinkered vision”. The classic cause is a tumor of the pituitary, which lies right below the chiasm.
<b>Повреждён правый зрительный тракт</b>: Right optic tract damaged (after the chiasm). It carries the fibers from both eyes that serve the left half of the field. Both eyes lose the left half: left homonymous hemianopia. The same happens with a stroke in the right occipital lobe.
<b>Повреждён левый зрительный тракт.</b>: Left optic tract damaged. Both eyes lose the right half of the field: right homonymous hemianopia.
Здоровый глаз: хрусталик сам меняет силу: A healthy eye: the lens adjusts its own power, and the image of both distant and near objects falls exactly on the retina.
<b>Близорукость (миопия):</b> глаз слишк: Nearsightedness (myopia): the eye is too long or its optics too strong. Rays from a distant object converge in front of the retina: distant things look blurry, while near ones are sharp. Corrected with diverging lenses (minus).
<b>Дальнозоркость (гиперметропия):</b> г: Farsightedness (hyperopia): the eye is a bit too short, and the focus falls behind the retina. The lens is constantly straining, and for near objects it runs out of power. Corrected with converging lenses (plus).
<b>Пресбиопия:</b> с возрастом хрусталик: Presbyopia: with age the lens hardens and almost stops changing shape. Distance vision is normal, but close-up text blurs: the focus slips behind the retina. Hence reading glasses after age 40–45.
